bib.title: ARK-V1: An LLM-Agent for Knowledge Graph Question Answering Requiring Commonsense Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "ARK-V1: An LLM-Agent for Knowledge Graph Question Answering Requiring Commonsense Reasoning", Jan-Felix Klein and Lars Ohnemus (KIT, Institute of Material Handling and Logistics), arXiv:2509.18063v1 [cs.CL], 22 Sep 2025. Preprint; the extraction shows no venue. Funded by DFG SFB 1574. Code: github.com/JaFeKl/ark_v1.

COVERAGE: All 23,405 of 23,405 chars read, every page, including references. Nothing skipped. Figure text was extracted as scrambled node labels, but the captions are readable. The paper has no appendices.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: ARK-V1 is a simple, non-fine-tuned KG agent. It loops through select anchor entity, select relation, retrieve triples and reason, then summarises. After each step it resets the context to the system prompt, the query and a running summary.
  number: none
  setup: The KG is a property graph of tuples (h, r, t, phi). The anchor must be a head entity in the graph. Relations must be outgoing edges of that anchor. Invalid picks are retried up to C_max. Exploration is capped at K_max steps.
  quote: "Reset the message context to include only the system prompt, the queryQ, and the generated summary"
  where: p.3, Sec. III.C
- Claim: With a Qwen3-30B backbone, ARK-V1 reaches about 91% conditional accuracy and about 70% overall accuracy, against 65-68% for the o1 CoT baselines. The two sets of numbers are not like for like.
  number: Qwen3-30B stochastic: 76.98 answer rate, 91.22 conditional, 70.20 overall, reliability 0.65. o1 zero-shot CoT: 97 answer rate, 65 conditional, 67 overall.
  setup: CoLoTa, 200 binary tasks. Qwen3-30B at T=0.7 over 30 runs. The o1 baselines are the CoLoTa authors' reported figures, labelled "Baseline results from external sources".
  quote: "It answers on average≈77% of questions while achieving a conditional accuracy above ≈91%, leading to an overall accuracy of≈70%."
  where: p.4-5, Tables II and III
- Claim: Large backbones all reach conditional accuracy above 94% and overall accuracy of about 70-74% at T=0, so scaling gives diminishing returns in conditional accuracy but better coverage and reliability. Mid-scale Qwen3-30B comes close.
  number: Qwen3-235B 71.5 / 95.80 / 68.5. Gemini 2.5 Flash 76.5 / 96.08 / 73.5. GPT-5 Mini 77 / 94.81 / 73. gpt-oss-125B 75 / 94.00 / 70.5. Qwen3-30B 79.5 / 93.08 / 74.0. Each triple is answer rate / conditional / overall, in %.
  setup: T=0, single run, CoLoTa. No variance is available for these rows.
  quote: "Across these large backbones, conditional accuracy consistently exceeds94%with overall accuracies around70-74%."
  where: p.4, Sec. V and Table III
- Claim: Small backbones abstain heavily, so overall accuracy collapses even though conditional accuracy is decent. Reliability rises with size.
  number: Qwen3-8B answer rate 57.67%, conditional 84.02%, overall 48.42%, reliability 0.52. Qwen3-14B answer rate 45.93%, overall 40.95%, reliability 0.57.
  setup: T=0.7, 30 runs, mean ± SD. Reliability is 1 − H/log2(3) over {True, False, None}, averaged over questions.
  quote: "the entropy-based reliability increases from0.52forQwen3-8Bto0.65forQwen3-30B"
  where: p.4, Table III
- Claim: CoT baselines almost never abstain and guess, which inflates coverage and hurts accuracy. The KG agent trades coverage for precision by answering None when the graph lacks the facts.
  number: o1 answer rate 97% (zero-shot) and 94% (few-shot).
  quote: "they often default to guessing rather than abstaining, which inflates coverage but comes at the cost of accuracy."
  where: p.4, Sec. V
- Claim: Three recurring error classes, from the authors' qualitative analysis: (i) ambiguous questions, where backbones interpret "speaking" differently; (ii) conflicting triples in the KG, where weaker models stop at the first path; (iii) over-reliance on KG evidence when commonsense is needed.
  number: none (anecdotal, with named dataset entries)
  setup: CoLoTa entries S4, S28, S75, 34, S193, S119, S163. Entry 34 is Mahmoud Dowlatabadi: Gemini 2.5 Flash fetched Kelidar directly and answered correctly. GPT-5-Mini and the Qwen3 8B, 30B and 80B models stopped at the "short story" triple and answered False.
  quote: "In these cases, the agent over-relies on KG evidence and fails to draw on widely available commonsense knowledge."
  where: p.4-5, Sec. V.A

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "token usage grows with exploration depth, redundant traversal of triples may occur, and prompting strategies remain relatively simple." Future work is efficiency, adaptive prompting, and domain graphs (robotics scene graphs, enterprise KGs).
- The only benchmark is CoLoTa (200 questions). There is no WebQSP, CWQ or GrailQA comparison with RoG, ToG or KG-Agent, even though Table I lists those datasets. The only baselines are o1 CoT numbers taken from the CoLoTa paper.
- The comparison is not like for like: ARK-V1 gets KG access and different backbones, o1 gets no KG. There is no ablation, no CoT baseline run on the same backbones, and no token or cost numbers.
- Temperature-0 rows have no variance. The paper gives no latency, step counts or prompts in the text.
- The paper says CoLoTa has ambiguous questions and conflicting evidence, so part of the accuracy ceiling is dataset noise.
- Retrieval is exact symbolic traversal of outgoing edges from one anchor at a time. There is no text-to-query step, no Cypher or SPARQL, and no backward (incoming) edges.
- It is a short preprint with no peer review shown.

BUILDS ON
- Method families: semantic parsing vs information retrieval, citing Ding et al. 2025 (J. Intelligent Information Systems).
- KG-agent line: Jiang et al. 2024, KG-Agent (arXiv 2402.11163); Luo et al. 2023, RoG, "Reasoning on Graphs" (arXiv 2310.01061); Sun et al. 2023, Think-on-Graph (arXiv 2307.07697); Guo et al. 2024, KnowledgeNavigator (Complex & Intelligent Systems 10.5); Baek et al. 2023, KAPING (NLRSE workshop); Li et al. 2023, triplet retrieval (arXiv 2305.18742).
- Property graph definition: Hogan et al. 2021, "Knowledge Graphs" (ACM Computing Surveys 54.4). Motivation: Pan et al. 2024, LLM+KG roadmap (IEEE TKDE).
- Dataset: Toroghi, Guo and Sanner, CoLoTa, SIGIR 2025. It adapts StrategyQA (Geva et al. 2021, TACL) and CREAK (Onoe et al. 2021).

CODE: none in the paper (the repo link is above).

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.2): "Agent Architecture of ARK-V1". This is the one figure candidate. It is an 11-node state graph with retry and abort routes, showing a bounded exploration loop with validity checks and a context reset. It fits note 01 or 05 on graph vs loop as well as note 11.
- Fig. 2 (p.3): CoLoTa example (Horsens vs Ikast population). It shows a two-hop KG lookup plus a commonsense comparison.

PROBLEMS
- The extraction shows no embedded instructions. Fig. 1 text is scrambled node labels. Math symbols are slightly garbled, for example "route" cases and "theCoLoTadataset" with spaces dropped. Quotes are copied as extracted.
- Note fit: the paper is an IR/agentic traversal method with no text-to-Cypher, so it fits 11-kg-rag-and-text-to-cypher.md only as the contrast case, "agent walks the graph step by step" against "generate a query". 11b-text-to-cypher-qa-agent.md is similar, but that note is about text-to-Cypher. If either note covers an agentic loop with retry and validity routing, I would add it there as an alternative. Note 12 is not relevant. The paper also fits the loop-with-validation idea in notes 01 and 05, but I did not read the notes, so this is only a pointer.
